video_title: INSIDE THE LOCKER ROOM: Josh Giddey's HISTORIC Performance in WILD Bulls OT Loss to Nuggets

quotes.speaker: Billy Donovan
quotes.summary_phrase: Billy Donovan on the Bulls' late-game execution against the Nuggets
quotes.excerpt: Murray, Gordon, Jokic, they took over the game and won it.
quotes.quote: I think both teams were tired in overtime. We were for sure, but they were also. Again, this is a very talented team. Murray, Gordon, Jokic, they took over the game and won it. I think it was a high-level offensive game tonight on both ends. We just couldn't finish.
quotes.social_post: Billy Donovan on the Bulls overtime loss to the Nuggets: We were tired and they were too, but Murray, Gordon, and Jokic took over the game and won it. We just could not finish.

structured.context: Billy Donovan discusses the Bulls' overtime loss to the Nuggets and credits the opposing players for their performance.

quotes.speaker: Billy Donovan
quotes.summary_phrase: Billy Donovan on the Bulls' struggle to secure defensive rebounds
quotes.excerpt: It's a big body, Jokic and Gordon, so we got to be able to box them out.
quotes.quote: It's part of one of our problems. You can go bigger, but also you're going to lose different things when you do that. We just got to be better. We got to be more mindful about the rebound. Of course, Gordon and Jokic were excellent in that part. One got six and one got five. I think that's the game right there in terms of possessions. It's a big body, Jokic and Gordon, so we got to be able to box them out.
quotes.social_post: Billy Donovan on the Bulls rebounding struggles against Denver: It is part of our problems. We have to be more mindful about the rebound and be able to box out big bodies like Jokic and Gordon.

structured.context: Billy Donovan explains the Bulls' struggles with defensive rebounding against the Nuggets' frontcourt.

quotes.speaker: Billy Donovan
quotes.summary_phrase: Billy Donovan on Noah's performance and potential for more minutes
quotes.excerpt: Did any part of you maybe consider like playing him more or down the stretch even in overtime?

text_blocks.speaker: Unidentified reporter
text_blocks.text: It felt like he gave some of the better efforts on the glass.

text_blocks.speaker: Billy Donovan
text_blocks.text: Did any part of you maybe consider like playing him more or down the stretch even in overtime? Yeah, I mean, I thought that other guys were doing a good job. He was kind of taking the ice minutes on the bench. I tried to mirror Murray minutes with with ice. Tough matchup, not easy. But yeah, maybe maybe Noah should play more.

quotes.social_post: Billy Donovan admits he maybe should have played Noah more down the stretch against the Nuggets: I thought other guys were doing a good job, but yeah, maybe Noah should play more.

structured.context: Billy Donovan reflects on his rotation decisions regarding a player's minutes during the game against the Nuggets.

quotes.speaker: Billy Donovan
quotes.summary_phrase: Billy Donovan praises Josh Giddey's performance against the Nuggets
quotes.excerpt: Josh played extremely well, 22 assists, 23 points.
quotes.quote: We got to talk about Josh game. He played extremely well, 22 assists, 23 points. We got to give them flowers when they deserve. Last game they didn't have it, tonight they brought it. So excellent game by both those two guys.
quotes.social_post: Billy Donovan on Josh Giddey's 23 point and 22 assist performance: We got to give them flowers when they deserve. Excellent game by both those two guys.

structured.context: Billy Donovan praises Josh Giddey for his individual performance in the game against the Nuggets.

quotes.speaker: Billy Donovan
quotes.summary_phrase: Billy Donovan on the Bulls' fourth-quarter response
quotes.excerpt: Against this team, you got to really take care of the non-Jokic minutes.
quotes.quote: We've been talking about that. We still lost the third quarter, but it wasn't as bad. I think we came back in the fourth. We had a good effort there. It's just against this team, you got to really take care of the non-Jokic minutes. He's excellent, and he plays the first quarter and the third quarter. So you know you got to try to survive those minutes. That's how good he is, honestly. And then you got to try to to beat the non-Jokic minutes. And tonight wasn't enough.
quotes.social_post: Billy Donovan on the challenge of playing the Nuggets: You have to try to survive the Jokic minutes. That is how good he is, honestly. And then you have to try to beat the non-Jokic minutes. Tonight was not enough.

structured.context: Billy Donovan discusses the tactical challenge of managing the game during the minutes Nikola Jokic is on the floor.

quotes.speaker: Josh Giddey
quotes.summary_phrase: Josh Giddey on the Bulls' resilience despite the loss
quotes.excerpt: I thought we we didn't let go of the rope, we battled and battled.
quotes.quote: They're a good team and they've been in all the instances before. They know how to handle different coverages. Jokic, Murray, probably seen it all, so they made shots. Deflating when you go down eight to start overtime. You don't have a lot of time to to claw back out of a out of a hole like that. So I thought we we didn't let go of the rope, we battled and battled, even during regulation. I think just just giving up eight quick ones in overtime, it's tough to come back from that, but I thought we we fought hard and played the right way and gave ourselves every chance to win that game.
quotes.social_post: Josh Giddey on the Bulls fighting back in the loss to Denver: It is deflating when you go down eight to start overtime. You do not have a lot of time to claw back out of a hole like that, but we did not let go of the rope.

structured.context: Josh Giddey describes the difficulty of overcoming an early deficit in overtime against a veteran Nuggets team.

quotes.speaker: Josh Giddey
quotes.summary_phrase: Josh Giddey on what the Bulls can learn from competitive losses
quotes.excerpt: It shows that we're there, like we have the ability to win and be in these good games.
quotes.quote: It shows that we're there, like we have the ability to win and be in these good games against good teams. Although the results haven't gone our way probably more more often than not this year, we've shown that we can compete and we can be competitive when we play the right way. It's just a matter of doing it for 48 minutes. I think we've shown stretches where we're really good and we've shown stretches where, you know, we can also lose to anybody in the league. So it's a matter of shortening those bad stretches and lengthening the good ones and we put ourselves in a position to win games against some of the best teams in the league.
quotes.social_post: Josh Giddey on the Bulls' season: We have shown we can compete when we play the right way. It is a matter of shortening those bad stretches and lengthening the good ones.

structured.context: Josh Giddey discusses the team's ability to remain competitive against top-tier opponents despite recent losses.

quotes.speaker: Josh Giddey
quotes.summary_phrase: Josh Giddey on Billy Donovan's communication and accountability
quotes.excerpt: He doesn't sugarcoat it, he tells you what you what you need, he not what you want to hear.
quotes.quote: That's one of the things about him, I think really good communicator. And he probably, you know, as a former player, he probably understands as well and he he can relate to us as players a lot more. And yeah, he was really good about it, I think. As he says, it's not the first time, but he doesn't sugarcoat it, he tells you what you what you need, he not what you want to hear. And you know, as players, it's frustrating in the moment, obviously you want to be out there trying to help your team win games, but I wasn't surprised, I wasn't sitting there confused as to why I wasn't out there. Like I knew why and he hit it on the head the next day and we move forward and move on to tonight.
quotes.social_post: Josh Giddey on Billy Donovan's coaching style: He does not sugarcoat it, he tells you what you need, not what you want to hear. I was not surprised when I was benched, I knew why and he hit it on the head.

structured.context: Josh Giddey explains how he appreciates Billy Donovan's direct communication and accountability, even when being benched.

quotes.speaker: Josh Giddey
quotes.summary_phrase: Josh Giddey on the lessons learned from being benched
quotes.excerpt: I mean, what not to do, I think that's what got us there in the first place.
quotes.quote: I mean, what not to do, I think that's what got us there in the first place. Both of us obviously want to be out there trying to help us win games and down the stretch when you're not out there, it's as I said, it's frustrating, but you've got to do your best to to cheer your team on and and root for the guys that are out there. And yeah, I mean, as I as I said, I mean, we we both want to be out there, but it's you know, that's not where we're out there playing, so we've got to perform the right way to be out there at the end of games.
quotes.social_post: Josh Giddey on being benched: It is frustrating, but you have to do your best to cheer your team on. We have to perform the right way to be out there at the end of games.

structured.context: Josh Giddey discusses the mental challenge of staying supportive of teammates while being benched during crunch time.

quotes.speaker: Josh Giddey
quotes.summary_phrase: Josh Giddey on Billy Donovan's culture of accountability
quotes.excerpt: He's not going at one or two guys, like everyone in the team is held accountable.
quotes.quote: Yeah, he does, and you can see it. Even during film and and things behind the scenes, like it's he's not going at one or two guys, like everyone in the team is held accountable and that's a that's a thing as as players you love. And as I said, he's a former player, so he understands it. You know, you've got to hold your best players accountable the same way you hold guys that probably aren't in the rotation accountable. So you look up and down the line and when we go through film and and and walk throughs and practices, everyone's held accountable to the same standard and that's how you get better as a team.
quotes.social_post: Josh Giddey on the culture in Chicago: Everyone in the team is held accountable and that is a thing as players you love. You have to hold your best players accountable the same way you hold guys that are not in the rotation.

structured.context: Josh Giddey praises the culture of accountability that Billy Donovan has established within the Bulls locker room.

quotes.speaker: Josh Giddey
quotes.summary_phrase: Josh Giddey on the Bulls' offensive improvement through ball movement
quotes.excerpt: A lot of it's just playing together. I think early in the year it was a lot of ISO.
quotes.quote: A lot of it's just playing together. I think early in the year it was a lot of ISO, a lot of one-on-one, a lot of bad early shots in the possession. And now we're starting to figure out, you know, how we're effective as an offense and as a team. And that's probably not the the answer for us. Like we've got a group where when we move the ball, we get into quick actions, we rebound and run, we we look good. So that stuff takes time when you put a bunch of new guys together, it takes time to figure out, but I think we're trending in the right direction.
quotes.social_post: Josh Giddey on the Bulls' offensive evolution: Early in the year it was a lot of ISO and bad early shots. Now we are figuring out how we are effective as a team. We are trending in the right direction.

structured.context: Josh Giddey explains how the Bulls' offense is improving through better ball movement compared to early-season isolation plays.

quotes.speaker: Ayo Dosunmu
quotes.summary_phrase: Ayo Dosunmu on the Bulls' need to close out games
quotes.excerpt: Our niche, I mean we need to get better at closing games.
quotes.quote: I know we team that building. I wouldn't say we're young. We got guys that have been in the league. You know, we just trying to figure out how to win and close out games. I think that's our that's our niche. I mean we need to get better at closing games. We're competing hard enough to be in games for the past eight or nine. Now it's just freaking hard to close now.
quotes.social_post: Ayo Dosunmu on the Bulls' struggles: We are just trying to figure out how to win and close out games. I think that is our niche. We need to get better at closing games.

structured.context: Ayo Dosunmu discusses the team's need to improve their ability to close out games in the final minutes.

quotes.speaker: Ayo Dosunmu
quotes.summary_phrase: Ayo Dosunmu on stepping up in the rotation
quotes.excerpt: Yeah, that too, but also uh thinking about the job opportunities given to me.

text_blocks.speaker: Unidentified reporter
text_blocks.text: You've been doing what you did tonight for a long time in this league, but when a guy like Norman's out and you get the start, do you try to be a little bit more aggressive looking for your shot?

text_blocks.speaker: Ayo Dosunmu
text_blocks.text: Yeah, that too, but also uh thinking about the job opportunities given to me. You know, I know my role in this team and I just come on and be professional and do my job and play and be vocal as I can each and every night and go there and compete when whatever minutes I get.

quotes.social_post: Ayo Dosunmu on his role: I know my role on this team and I just come on and be professional and do my job and play and be as vocal as I can each and every night.

structured.context: Ayo Dosunmu discusses his professional approach to his role and his readiness to step up when given more minutes.

quotes.speaker: Ayo Dosunmu
quotes.summary_phrase: Ayo Dosunmu on the Bulls' early-season shooting struggles
quotes.excerpt: You know when you in a rut, you know you just got to figure it out.
quotes.quote: You know when you in a rut, you know you just got to figure it out. You know it's never going to be easy, and it's never going to be perfect. You just got to figure it out. Life is always never easy. It's never nobody nobody has a perfect life. You know, we we all go through stuff and that's our basketball right where we're in and we're coming out of that and we're competing and we're giving the fans something that they've been longing to see.
quotes.social_post: Ayo Dosunmu on the team's shooting slump: When you are in a rut, you just have to figure it out. It is never going to be easy and it is never going to be perfect. Life is never easy.

structured.context: Ayo Dosunmu reflects on the team's process of working through early-season struggles and shooting slumps.

quotes.speaker: Ayo Dosunmu
quotes.summary_phrase: Ayo Dosunmu on the Bulls' recent success against All-NBA players
quotes.excerpt: This is the NBA, you do want to play against the best, you want to compete against the best.

text_blocks.speaker: Unidentified reporter
text_blocks.text: Is there any significance that you've played a succession of all NBA players, you know, MVPs, potential MVPs?

text_blocks.speaker: Ayo Dosunmu
text_blocks.text: No, excuse me, why am I going to feel sorry for you? You know, no matter who is on the court, like you love the opportunities given to you. That's why we here, why we competing. This is the NBA, you do want to play against the best, you want to compete against the best. And I think that the our everybody is answering the bell, especially Mada and Josh. They're they're turning up a lot.

quotes.social_post: Ayo Dosunmu on facing elite talent: This is the NBA, you do want to play against the best. Everybody is answering the bell, especially Matas and Josh. They are turning up a lot.

structured.context: Ayo Dosunmu expresses the team's excitement to compete against the best players in the NBA.

quotes.speaker: Ayo Dosunmu
quotes.summary_phrase: Ayo Dosunmu on the importance of communication from the coach
quotes.excerpt: Who doesn't like a great coach, a coach that communicates? I think every player loves that.

text_blocks.speaker: Unidentified reporter
text_blocks.text: You mentioned a couple times you've been benched before, you've talked to Josh or Mada about what it was like and how they get how you got out of it or how you developed and what you learned?

text_blocks.speaker: Ayo Dosunmu
text_blocks.text: No, I haven't talked to them, but I'm sure we all no matter what, how long we've been in this league, we all coach that process where you're you're in the starting lineup or you can get benched. And it's up to you what you do with it. Who doesn't like a great coach, a coach that communicates? I think every player loves that. And I think that once you once he's directing and communicating that, I think you feel better about yourself and better where you're going.

quotes.social_post: Ayo Dosunmu on coaching communication: Who does not like a great coach, a coach that communicates? I think every player loves that. Once he is directing and communicating, you feel better about yourself.

structured.context: Ayo Dosunmu discusses the importance of having a coach who communicates clearly with players regarding their roles.
